# The US federal debt limit as dated data - the statute's steps, the 2025 reinstatement reproduced, the record's last extraordinary measures, Treasury's perimeters (PS-6 US-14)

Read on the files the stamp names (`ElectionsData/usa/raw/treasury_debt/`, `raw/debt_limit/`, `raw/budget_statutes/`; the reading is `ElectionsData/usa/debt_limit.md`). Treasury's tables give USD millions; a figure here is that figure times a million, nothing rounded. `UsDebtLimitCheck` (the cheap bar) recomputes every Treasury figure below from the same files and fails while this document differs.

## The reinstatement of 2 January 2025, reproduced from the record's own debt

P.L. 118-5 s401(b): the limit in force, raised by the face amount outstanding on 2 January 2025 less that outstanding on the date of enactment. Debt subject to limit from the Daily Treasury Statement's table III-C (whole USD millions as published; held by the public + intragovernmental - the three lines not subject + guaranteed debt):

- the limit in force on the date of enactment: **31,381,463** mil (the DTS's limit line on 2 June 2023);
- outstanding on the date of enactment (3 June 2023, a Saturday - the Friday's close, the Monday's opening): **31,381,438** mil;
- outstanding on 2 January 2025, read as Treasury read it - "at the end of the previous day" (the Secretary's letter of 27 December 2024, read from the page image): 2 January's opening, **36,103,970** mil (31 December's close);
- reproduced: 31,381,463 + 36,103,970 - 31,381,438 = **36,103,995 mil**, against Treasury's **36,103,995,660,231** - within the three whole-million roundings (-0.660231 mil apart).
- 2 January's CLOSE (36,053,621 mil, after the redemption the letter names) would have given 36,053,646 mil - 50,349 mil lower: the formula reads the day's opening.
- To the dollar: MSPD table 2's debt subject to limit on 31 December 2024 is 36,103,970,650,921.5, the same close to a fraction of a dollar; so s401(b) carried a headroom of **25,009,309.5** (Treasury's limit less that debt), and the enactment-day debt Treasury's figure implies is 31,381,437,990,690.5, inside the DTS's whole million.
- With P.L. 119-21's $5,000,000,000,000: **41,103,995,660,231**.

## The record's last extraordinary measures (R-US21 (iii))

- **Reached 2025-01-21, ended 2025-07-04: 164 days.** Treasury's report on the CSRDF (30 January 2026): "On January 21, 2025, the outstanding debt subject to the limit reached the statutory debt limit"; the episode ended with P.L. 119-21. The DTS agrees: 12,954 mil under the limit on 2025-01-17, 26 under on 2025-01-21 and 26 under on 2025-07-03; on 2025-07-07 the limit line reads 41,103,996.
- **Projected to run out in August 2025: 192 to 222 days from 2025-01-21.** The Secretary's letter of 9 May 2025 (page image, no text layer): "there is a reasonable probability that the federal government's cash and extraordinary measures will be exhausted in August". The month is the reading; its first and last days bound it.
- **The measures' size on the first day: $338 billion** - Treasury's daily table ("Debt Subject to Limit - Extraordinary Measures", 3 July 2025), the January 21, 2025 row, Totals "Total Measures" (CSRDF/PSRHBF 19 + G Fund 299 + ESF 20).
- The 2023 episode, for the range: the DTS first shows the debt at the limit on 2023-01-19; P.L. 118-5 suspended it on 2023-06-03 - 135 days.
